Converts Alpine Linux SecDB security data into OVAL `models.Definition` structs by mapping CVE IDs to affected packages.

## Key Components

### `ConvertToModel(data *SecDB) []models.Definition`

Parses an Alpine `SecDB` structure and produces a slice of `models.Definition`, one per unique CVE ID found across all packages. Each definition includes:

- A deterministic `DefinitionID` formatted as `def-<reponame>-<distroversion>-<CVEИД>`
- A `models.Advisory` with a CVE reference link to `cve.mitre.org`
- All affected packages and their fix versions
- Stripped detail fields when the `no-details` Viper flag is set

## Usage Example

```go
secDB := &alpine.SecDB{
    Reponame:      "main",
    Distroversion: "v3.18",
    Packages: []alpine.Package{
        {
            Pkg: alpine.Pkg{
                Name: "openssl",
                Secfixes: map[string][]string{
                    "3.1.2-r0": {"CVE-2023-1234"},
                },
            },
        },
    },
}

defs := alpine.ConvertToModel(secDB)
// defs[0].DefinitionID == "def-main-v3.18-CVE-2023-1234"
// defs[0].AffectedPacks[0].Name == "openssl"
// defs[0].AffectedPacks[0].Version == "3.1.2-r0"
```

## Notes

- Only entries with IDs prefixed by `"CVE"` are processed; non-CVE entries (e.g. `XSA-*`) are skipped
- Multiple packages sharing the same CVE are grouped under a single `Definition`
- When `--no-details` is passed, advisory metadata (severity, bugzillas, CPEs, timestamps, references) is cleared to reduce storage footprint
